display.purpose: Short, shouted hero titles on story, Lineup, store, and tournament surfaces.

headline.purpose: Section and result headings with a tightly balanced measure.

title.purpose: Relic names, Move names, offer names, and prominent values.

body.purpose: Readable rules, descriptions, dialogue, and supporting instructions.

label.purpose: Uppercase class, provenance, meter, status, and control metadata.

shadows.name: ticket-lift
shadows.purpose: Standard structural lift beneath removable paper tickets and rails.

shadows.name: rail-lift
shadows.purpose: Shallow separation beneath the sticky application rail.

shadows.name: drawer-channel
shadows.purpose: Paired inset edges that make the battle stage read as an open collector drawer.

shadows.name: result-lift
shadows.purpose: Highest elevation, reserved for the blocking battle result stamp.

motion.name: meter-response
motion.purpose: Keeps health and Charge Strip values responsive without decorative easing.

motion.name: idle-swap
motion.purpose: Alternates paired rectangular idle prints when reduced motion is not active.

motion.name: print-echo-pulse
motion.purpose: Laterally displaces enlarged low-opacity still layers to create deliberate print misregistration.

motion.name: hit-nudge
motion.purpose: A short directional impact displacement paired with a stamped damage float.

motion.name: kinetic-cut-in
motion.purpose: Slams a selected Move print across the full arena before the lunge and impact.

motion.name: battle-countdown
motion.purpose: Owns the full stage while timer, Charge, AI, statuses, and commands remain frozen.

motion.name: presentation-lock
motion.value: 340ms to 1000ms fixed by semantic event type
motion.purpose: Keeps the complete simulation frozen until the authored cut-in, impact, switch, or KO presentation completes.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Collapses CSS transition and animation duration for system or explicit reduced-motion preferences.

components.name: Primary Print Button
components.description: The decisive action label for continuing, fighting, buying, or retrying.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { min-height: 3.6rem; border: 3px solid var(--ink, #14151a); padding: 0.72rem 1.2rem; background: var(--yellow, #f2d742); color: var(--ink, #14151a); box-shadow: 0.4rem 0.5rem 0.95rem rgb(4 8 22 / 35%); font-family: var(--display, "League Gothic", "Arial Narrow", sans-serif); font-size: 1.8rem; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--tomato, #ef4d39); color: var(--chalk, #f7f0dd); transform: translate(-1px, -1px); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 4px solid var(--focus, #8de1ff); outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translate(0, 0); }

components.name: Secondary Indigo Button
components.description: A quieter boxed action that remains legible against result and content sheets.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { min-height: 3.4rem; border: 3px solid var(--chalk, #f7f0dd); padding: 0.65rem 1rem; background: var(--indigo, #111f46); color: var(--chalk, #f7f0dd); font-family: var(--body, "Atkinson Hyperlegible", ui-sans-serif, sans-serif); font-weight: 700; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: var(--tomato, #ef4d39); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 4px solid var(--focus, #8de1ff); outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-btn-secondary:active { transform: translateY(1px); }

components.name: Game Mode Launcher
components.description: Three explicit session bills that explain Story, sandbox, and tournament consequences before entry.
components.html:
STORY MODE

Progress your collection through First Run.

QUICK FIGHT

Sandbox play with no Story rewards changed.

TOURNAMENT

A separate three-round persistent Case.
components.css: .ds-launcher { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1.35fr 0.65fr 0.65fr; gap: 1rem; background: var(--indigo-deep, #091128); padding: 1rem; } .ds-mode { display: grid; align-content: center; gap: 0.75rem; border: 5px solid var(--ink, #14151a); padding: 1.5rem; background: var(--chalk, #f7f0dd); color: var(--ink, #14151a); box-shadow: 0.55rem 0.7rem 1.25rem rgb(4 8 22 / 35%); } .ds-mode-quick { background: var(--yellow, #f2d742); } .ds-mode h2 { margin: 0; font-family: var(--display, "League Gothic", "Arial Narrow", sans-serif); font-size: 3rem; line-height: 0.86; } .ds-mode p { margin: 0; font-family: var(--body, "Atkinson Hyperlegible", ui-sans-serif, sans-serif); line-height: 1.4; } .ds-mode button { min-height: 2.8rem; border: 3px solid var(--ink, #14151a); background: var(--indigo, #111f46); color: var(--chalk, #f7f0dd); font-weight: 700; cursor: pointer; } .ds-mode button:hover { background: var(--tomato, #ef4d39); } .ds-mode button:focus-visible { outline: 4px solid var(--focus, #8de1ff); outline-offset: 3px; } @media (max-width: 620px) { .ds-launcher { grid-template-columns: 1fr; gap: 0.45rem; padding: 0.8rem; } .ds-mode { border-width: 3px; padding: 0.75rem; box-shadow: 0.2rem 0.25rem 0 var(--ink, #14151a); } .ds-mode h2 { font-size: 2.35rem; } }

components.name: Context Navigation Rail
components.description: A context-specific rail: this global example exposes Main Menu, Profile, Settings, and persisted music intent; Story swaps in its own destinations.
components.css: .ds-global-rail { display: flex; border: 4px solid var(--ink, #14151a); background: var(--chalk, #f7f0dd); } .ds-nav { display: flex; flex: 1; } .ds-nav-tab { min-width: 6rem; flex: 1; border: 0; border-right: 2px dashed rgb(20 21 26 / 36%); padding: 0.8rem 0.65rem; background: transparent; color: var(--indigo, #111f46); font-family: var(--body, "Atkinson Hyperlegible", ui-sans-serif, sans-serif); font-weight: 700; cursor: pointer; } .ds-nav-tab:hover, .ds-nav-tab.ds-is-active { background: var(--yellow, #f2d742); color: var(--ink, #14151a); } .ds-nav-tab.ds-is-active { box-shadow: inset 0 -0.45rem 0 var(--tomato, #ef4d39); } .ds-nav-tab:focus-visible, .ds-music:focus-visible { outline: 4px solid var(--focus, #8de1ff); outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-music { width: 3.5rem; border: 0; border-left: 3px solid var(--ink, #14151a); background: var(--tomato, #ef4d39); color: var(--chalk, #f7f0dd); font-size: 1.25rem; cursor: pointer; } .ds-music[aria-pressed="true"] { background: var(--indigo, #111f46); }

components.name: Registration Field
components.description: A plain paper field held by a hard registration border.
components.html: <label class="ds-field-label" for="ds-collector">COLLECTOR NAME</label><input class="ds-field" id="ds-collector" value="Collector" />
components.css: .ds-field-label { display: block; margin-bottom: 0.35rem; color: var(--ink, #14151a); font-family: var(--body, "Atkinson Hyperlegible", ui-sans-serif, sans-serif); font-size: 0.72rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.08em; } .ds-field { width: 100%; min-height: 2.8rem; border: 3px solid var(--ink, #14151a); border-radius: 0; padding: 0.45rem 0.65rem; background: #fff; color: var(--ink, #14151a); font-family: var(--body, "Atkinson Hyperlegible", ui-sans-serif, sans-serif); } .ds-field:hover { border-color: var(--tomato, #ef4d39); } .ds-field:focus-visible { outline: 4px solid var(--focus, #8de1ff); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Lineup Specimen Ticket
components.description: A roster ticket combining square character art, class, health, and explicit state.
components.css: .ds-lineup-ticket { position: relative; display: grid; width: 18rem; min-height: 5.4rem; grid-template-columns: 4rem minmax(0, 1fr); gap: 0.6rem; align-items: center; border: 3px solid var(--ink, #14151a); padding: 0.35rem; overflow: hidden; background: var(--chalk, #f7f0dd); color: var(--ink, #14151a); text-align: left; clip-path: polygon(0 0, 100% 0, 100% calc(100% - 0.55rem), calc(100% - 0.55rem) 100%, 0 100%); cursor: pointer; } .ds-lineup-ticket:hover { background: var(--yellow, #f2d742); transform: translateX(0.2rem); } .ds-lineup-ticket:focus-visible { outline: 4px solid var(--focus, #8de1ff); outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-lineup-art { display: grid; width: 4rem; height: 4rem; place-items: center; background: var(--indigo, #111f46); color: var(--chalk, #f7f0dd); font-family: var(--display, "League Gothic", "Arial Narrow", sans-serif); font-size: 2.5rem; } .ds-lineup-copy { display: grid; font-family: var(--body, "Atkinson Hyperlegible", ui-sans-serif, sans-serif); } .ds-lineup-copy strong { font-size: 1rem; } .ds-lineup-copy small { font-size: 0.72rem; } .ds-lineup-state { position: absolute; right: -1.6rem; bottom: 0.45rem; width: 6rem; background: var(--indigo, #111f46); color: var(--chalk, #f7f0dd); font-size: 0.62rem; font-weight: 700; text-align: center; transform: rotate(-38deg); }

components.name: Battle Move Seal
components.description: One of three equal circular actions pinned directly above its exact position on the Charge rail.
components.css: .ds-move { display: grid; width: 8.2rem; justify-items: center; border: 0; background: transparent; color: var(--chalk, #f7f0dd); font-family: var(--display, "League Gothic", "Arial Narrow", sans-serif); cursor: pointer; } .ds-move-seal { position: relative; display: grid; width: 5rem; height: 5rem; place-content: center; border: 0.32rem solid var(--ink, #14151a); border-radius: 50%; background: var(--charge-green, #8eef5d); color: var(--ink, #14151a); box-shadow: 0 0 0 0.25rem var(--chalk, #f7f0dd), 0 0 0 0.48rem var(--ink, #14151a), 0.34rem 0.4rem 0 0.46rem #48bf36; } .ds-move-seal strong { font-size: 2.45rem; line-height: 0.8; } .ds-move-seal small { font-family: var(--body, "Atkinson Hyperlegible", ui-sans-serif, sans-serif); font-size: 0.58rem; font-weight: 700; } .ds-move-key { position: absolute; right: 50%; bottom: -0.5rem; display: grid; width: 1.55rem; height: 1.55rem; place-items: center; border: 2px solid var(--ink, #14151a); border-radius: 50%; background: var(--chalk, #f7f0dd); transform: translateX(50%); } .ds-move-name { margin-top: 0.42rem; font-size: 1.25rem; text-shadow: 2px 2px 0 var(--ink, #14151a); } .ds-move-state { border: 2px solid var(--ink, #14151a); padding: 0.05rem 0.3rem; background: var(--charge-green, #8eef5d); color: var(--ink, #14151a); font-family: var(--body, "Atkinson Hyperlegible", ui-sans-serif, sans-serif); font-size: 0.58rem; font-weight: 700; } .ds-move:hover .ds-move-seal { transform: translateY(-0.25rem) rotate(-2deg); } .ds-move:focus-visible { outline: 4px solid var(--focus, #8de1ff); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Player Charge Strip
components.description: The full-width player resource immediately below the three Moves, including named cost thresholds.
components.html: YOUR CHARGE62 / 100
components.css: .ds-charge-deck { position: relative; width: min(64rem, 100%); padding: 0; color: var(--chalk, #f7f0dd); font-family: var(--body, "Atkinson Hyperlegible", ui-sans-serif, sans-serif); } .ds-charge-heading { position: absolute; z-index: 2; right: 0.55rem; bottom: 0.52rem; left: 0.55rem; display: flex; justify-content: space-between; font-weight: 700; pointer-events: none; } .ds-charge-heading span, .ds-charge-heading strong { border: 2px solid var(--chalk, #f7f0dd); padding: 0.1rem 0.35rem; background: var(--indigo-deep, #091128); } .ds-charge-heading strong { color: var(--charge-green, #8eef5d); font-family: var(--display, "League Gothic", "Arial Narrow", sans-serif); font-size: 1.45rem; } .ds-meter { height: 3.25rem; border: 0.38rem solid var(--ink, #14151a); overflow: hidden; background: var(--indigo-soft, #1a326a); box-shadow: 0 0 0 0.2rem var(--focus, #8de1ff), 0.38rem 0.45rem 0 0.2rem var(--ink, #14151a); } .ds-meter span { display: block; width: 100%; height: 100%; background: var(--charge-green, #8eef5d); box-shadow: inset -0.5rem 0 0 #48bf36; transform: scaleX(var(--ds-fill, 0)); transform-origin: left center; transition: transform 80ms linear; }

components.name: Status Stamp
components.description: An outlined text label for battle status that never relies on colour alone.
components.css: .ds-status { display: inline-block; border: 2px solid var(--ink, #14151a); padding: 0.06rem 0.35rem; background: var(--chalk, #f7f0dd); color: var(--ink, #14151a); font-family: var(--body, "Atkinson Hyperlegible", ui-sans-serif, sans-serif); font-size: 0.62rem; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-status:hover { background: var(--yellow, #f2d742); } .ds-status:focus-visible { outline: 4px solid var(--focus, #8de1ff); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Battle Result Stamp
components.description: The blocking, highest-elevation verdict sheet shown after a fight.
components.css: .ds-result { width: min(38rem, 100%); border: 6px solid var(--ink, #14151a); padding: 2rem; overflow: hidden; background: var(--yellow, #f2d742); color: var(--ink, #14151a); box-shadow: 0.8rem 1rem 2rem rgb(0 0 0 / 50%); transform: rotate(-0.6deg); font-family: var(--body, "Atkinson Hyperlegible", ui-sans-serif, sans-serif); } .ds-result > span { font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.08em; } .ds-result h2 { max-width: 10ch; margin: 0.8rem 0; font-family: var(--display, "League Gothic", "Arial Narrow", sans-serif); font-size: 4rem; line-height: 0.88; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-result dl { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); margin: 0; border: 4px solid currentColor; } .ds-result dl div { display: grid; padding: 0.65rem; border-right: 3px dashed currentColor; } .ds-result dl div:last-child { border-right: 0; } .ds-result dt { font-size: 0.68rem; font-weight: 700; } .ds-result dd { margin: 0; font-family: var(--display, "League Gothic", "Arial Narrow", sans-serif); font-size: 2.4rem; }

narrative.overview:
loftwah/fighter feels like a pulled-open collector drawer full of underground fight bills, specimen labels, scuffed toys, and hand-stamped results. It is tactile, dense, irreverent, and immediately playable: the interface behaves like a physical archive being sorted under pressure, never like a floating sci-fi HUD.

The visual world uses a constrained risograph palette, blunt display type, torn seams, clipped paper corners, halftone texture, and square pull-tabs. The player enters through an explicit three-mode launcher, then sees navigation scoped to the chosen game context. Static rectangular character art becomes kinetic through layered stills, two-frame swaps, panel translation, cut-ins, hit-stop, shake, flashes, and stamped feedback. Story's durable interaction loop is story node → Lineup → Charge Strip → Stamps → next print.
keyCharacteristics: Pulled-open drawer composition with compact rails and strict trays.
Three explicit game-mode bills before any session begins.
Separate global and Story-scoped navigation rails.
Indigo board, tomato and acid-yellow spot inks, chalk stock, and near-black registration ink.
Layered rectangular Kinetic Print stills with halftone wear and purposeful misregistration.
Square, bordered controls with torn or clipped paper edges; circles are reserved for holes and stamps.
Large condensed uppercase display type paired with highly legible body copy.
Short, forceful motion that always has a reduced-motion equivalent.

rules.name: The Spot-Ink Rule
rules.body: Tomato and acid yellow signal action or state; do not spend them as ambient decoration.

rules.name: The Registration Rule
rules.body: Light paper objects are held together by visible near-black borders, seams, or dividers.

rules.name: The Cyan Exception Rule
rules.body: Focus cyan belongs to keyboard focus only and must not become a general accent.

rules.name: The Shout-and-Explain Rule
rules.body: League Gothic names the thing; Atkinson Hyperlegible explains what it does.

rules.name: The Short Display Rule
rules.body: Display copy stays brief and balanced—headlines are labels, not paragraphs.

rules.name: The Arena-First Rule
rules.body: Compress labels and secondary metadata before reducing the central art stage below a usable decision surface.

rules.name: The Pinned-Control Rule
rules.body: Health, timer, Lineups, Pause, and the Move-and-Charge field attach to screen edges so the arena never becomes a small card inside UI chrome.

rules.name: The Three-Move Rule
rules.body: All three Moves remain equally prominent; no action receives a privileged hero-card slot.

rules.name: The Explicit Launch Rule
rules.body: Story, Quick Fight, and Tournament begin or resume only from a deliberate launcher action.

rules.name: The Context Rail Rule
rules.body: Global navigation and Story navigation are separate; Store and Missions never leak into global, Quick Fight, or standalone Tournament context.

rules.name: The Charge-First Rule
rules.body: The player reads one large Charge Strip and the three Move seals anchored to it as a single control. Moves must never drift into a separate row of dashboard cards.

rules.name: The Printed-Object Rule
rules.body: A shadow represents a physical label or drawer layer, never a generic floating panel.

rules.name: The No-Glass Rule
rules.body: Tonal opacity may support legibility over art, but blur, glow, and glassmorphism do not belong in this world.

rules.name: The Layered-Still Rule
rules.body: Build spectacle by composing and displacing static prints; never disguise limited-frame art with generic particle noise.

rules.name: The Square-First Rule
rules.body: Start every surface at zero radius; earn a circle only when it represents a physical punch, stamp, or control.

rules.name: The Controlled-Crooked Rule
rules.body: Rotation stays subtle on cards and forceful only on explicit stamps; content alignment remains readable.

rules.name: The Persistent Intent Rule
rules.body: Turning music off is durable user intent, not a temporary state for the current screen.

rules.name: The Touch Explanation Rule
rules.body: Responsive compression may shorten Move output to a compact hit/effect summary, but it may not remove the explanation entirely.

rules.name: The Choose-Then-Watch Rule
rules.body: A command is selected before its presentation. No further player or AI decision may be accepted while that presentation owns the stage.

rules.name: The Still-Image-Camera Rule
rules.body: Static art earns energy through entrance slides, asymmetric framing, scale changes, diagonal panels, cut-ins, hit reactions, damage stamps, and decisive camera resets—not ambient particles or constant wandering.

dos: Do stage play as labelled physical matter: drawers, tickets, specimen wells, pull-tabs, perforations, and stamps.
Do open on the explicit three-mode launcher and preserve the selected session context until the player exits it.
Do keep the first battle viewport readable as top health, edge Lineups, dominant arena art, then the large integrated Move-and-Charge field.
Do freeze the complete simulation during countdowns and attack presentations while letting presentation motion finish.
Do use layered rectangular and square art as an intentional Kinetic Print language.
Do retain a readable short Move explanation on touch layouts and a fuller explanation on hover or keyboard focus.
Do pair colour with text, shape, position, or value for every gameplay state.
Do preserve visible keyboard focus, touch-sized controls, and the reduced-motion override.
Do preserve the player's music on/off intent across navigation, reloads, and Collector profiles.
Do use stable logical asset IDs and the approved fallback chain when adding new art.
donts: Don't introduce rounded dashboard cards, pills as default controls, glassmorphism, neon glow, or a sci-fi HUD.
Don't turn tomato or acid yellow into unbounded decoration; they communicate action and state.
Don't obscure the arena with floating panels or let opposing readouts collide with the matchup stamp.
Don't allow Charge, timers, status durations, AI, or commands to advance behind a countdown or attack cut-in.
Don't mix global navigation with Story-only destinations such as Store or Missions.
Don't start Story, Quick Fight, Tournament, or music playback merely because a screen rendered.
Don't make one Move visually dominant over the other two.
Don't separate the player's Moves from the Charge Strip or hide all Move explanation on touch.
Don't rely on colour alone for class, status, availability, health, or outcome.
Don't add decorative motion without a short purpose and a reduced-motion equivalent.
